newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-DETROIT ADVANCES, DALLAS AND ANAHEIM FORCE SEVENTH GAMES.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-DETROIT ADVANCES, DALLAS AND ANAHEIM FORCE SEVENTH GAMES.

text.p: Brendan Shanahan's power-play goal 67 seconds into the second period snapped a 1-1 tie and propelled the Detroit Red Wings to a 3-1 win Sunday that eliminated the St Louis Blues from the Stanley Cup playoffs.
Detroit advanced to the Western Conference semifinals by capturing the best-of-seven first-round series four games to two as they eliminated the Blues for the second year in a row.
Two other Western Conference series were extended to climactic seventh games by visiting teams that staved off elimination.
The Dallas Stars beat the Edmonton Oilers 3-2, and the Mighty Ducks of Anaheim defeated the Phoenix Coyotes 3-2 in overtime to send their respective series to the limit.
In St Louis, Vyacheslav Kozlov and Kirk Maltby also scored for the triumphant Red Wings, who had two power-play goals for the second consecutive game.
Mike Vernon stopped 24 shots for Detroit in earning his 61st career playoff victory.
Brett Hull accounted for the St. Louis offence, staking the Blues to a 1-0 lead 2:12 into the contest.

The Red Wings' "Russian Unit" tied the game on the power play with 11:15 left in the first period. Igor Larionov dug the puck out of the right corner and gave it to Sergei Fedorov at the point. Fedorov slid a pass to Kozlov, who zipped a quick, low shot that went between Fuhr's pads.

After Shanahan slammed home a rebound to give Detroit the lead, St Louis had an apparent tying goal disallowed in the second period when video replays showed Pierre Turgeon's left skate was in the crease before he slid a rebound under Vernon in the final minute of the second period.
Grant Fuhr stopped 27 shots for St Louis, who were ousted in the opening round for the third time in four years.
Maltby scored an insurance goal with 11:36 to play.
In Edmonton, Mike Modano scored with 5:18 left to break a tie as the Dallas Stars forced a decisive seventh game with a 3-2 victory over the Edmonton Oilers in their series.

Dallas will host Game Seven on Tuesday. The Stars, who won the Central Division and is the second seed in the West, had the best road record in the league this season and posted their second win of the series in Edmonton.

"I haven't been around this level for very long, but this is the best hockey I've ever been involved with," Dallas coach Ken Hitchcock said. "It's been a hell of a series and if they put it in a boxed set and sell it, I'll buy a copy."
"This was, likely, the best-played game of the series," Edmonton coach Ron Low said. "Both teams played their 'A' game."

With the teams playing four skaters a side, Modano gained the puck in the right corner, went behind the net and skated around the perimeter before going into the slot, where his wrist shot went off the stick of Edmonton's Ryan Smyth and into the bottom right corner of the net past Curtis Joseph.
Modano has four goals in the series.

The Oilers pulled Joseph in the final minute but managed just one quality scoring chance. Smyth found Mike Grier at the right doorstep, but he shot the puck wide left and Andy Moog did not have to make a save.
Moog finished 33 saves and Joseph had 38.
"The fact that the road team has won four of the first six games shows how hard both teams are working," said Moog.
In Phoenix, Paul Kariya scored his second goal of the game at 7:29 of overtime and the Mighty Ducks of Anaheim forced a seventh game in their playoff series with a 3-2 win over the Phoenix Coyotes.

Teemu Selanne flipped the puck from his own zone across the Phoenix blue line, where it hopped over the stick of Coyotes defenceman Gerald Diduck. Kariya picked it up and wristed a shot from the left faceoff circle that beat Nikolai Khabibulin high to the stick side.
Anaheim, which was 3-0-13 in overtime during the regular season, will host Game Seven on Tuesday.
The Ducks squandered a two-goal lead in the third period as Phoenix, who had won the last three games in the series, rallied to force overtime on goals by Darrin Shannon and Keith Tkachuk.
Khabibulin made 36 saves for the Coyotes, who were outshot 39-21.
